events.text: TD34, 270,000 t Gulf of Oman to China, first assessed (WS197) as an alternative to TD3C on public trial

sources_line: Baltic Exchange weekly tanker reports; Breakwave Advisors tanker reports (via Hellenic Shipping News); Amplify Commodity Trust filings (SEC); EIA. Retrieved to 17 November 2026.

weekly.note: The report gives a range, WS57.5 to WS58; its upper end is recorded.

In that vein, while mostly theoretical, the TD3C route (270,000 mt Middle East Gulf to China) is being assessed 248 points higher than a week ago at WS473. While the Straits of Hormuz are not officially closed and the risk remains heightened, Baltic’s panellists feel able to price Middle East loading for the crude oil shipping market.

VLCC As the USA & Israeli action against Iran continued, an extraordinarily difficult week was experienced for the Baltic panellists. At present, our panellists remain able to price Middle East loading for the Crude Oil shipping market.

VLCC The continuing situation in the Middle East has meant challenges for the Baltic panellists. The extreme risk to shipping via the Strait of Hormuz still exists, however, our panellists remain able to price Middle East loading for the Crude Oil shipping market.

VLCC The ongoing situation in the Middle East is still causing the Baltic panellists some difficulties in assessing the Baltic routes from the region. As transits through the Strait of Hormuz are extremely limited, this route offers some semblance of a viable risk attitude for owners and charterers alike.
Transits through the Straits of Hormuz are extremely limited still, with owners and charterers seemingly unwilling to risk it.
VLCC Transits through the Straits of Hormuz remain limited, with reports this week of a blockade by the US Navy.
VLCC The Middle East situation continues with both the US and Iran claiming the Strait of Hormuz blocked, followed by reports of vessels transiting.
